title: Minimum Total Space Wasted With K Resizing Operations
summary: Given a sequence of element counts over time in the array nums, and a limit k on the number of resizing operations, determine the smallest total space wasted by resizing the array at most k times.
statement: Given a sequence of element counts over time in the array nums, and a limit k on the number of resizing operations, determine the smallest total space wasted by resizing the array at most k times. The array's size at any time t must be at least nums[t] to accommodate all elements, and the space wasted at time t is the difference between the array's size and the number of elements at that time. The total space wasted is the sum of these differences across all times. The array can be resized to any size, but only k times are allowed, and resizing does not count towards the k limit.
constraints: nums has 1 through 200 positive values, each at most 1000000.
0 <= k < len(nums); the initial array size is free and you may resize at most k times.
At each time the chosen capacity must be at least nums[t], and waste is capacity-nums[t].
hints: Once resize boundaries are fixed, each segment's cheapest legal capacity is its maximum demand.
Precompute every segment's waste, then partition the prefix into at most k+1 segments with dynamic programming.
The segment maximum is necessary and sufficient capacity. Trying every final split enumerates every legal resize schedule, and extra zero-benefit splits mean using exactly up to k+1 groups is safe.
editorial: The segment maximum is necessary and sufficient capacity. Trying every final split enumerates every legal resize schedule, and extra zero-benefit splits mean using exactly up to k+1 groups is safe.

tests.explanation: One capacity must cover both times, so capacity twenty wastes ten in total.
Three constant-capacity segments can achieve total waste fifteen.
